# The Center for Applied Postphenomenology

> An independent research center (est. 2026) collecting first-person accounts of life before and after the screen, to study how technologically and algorithmically mediated life has changed language, perception, society and what it means to be human.

Tagline: Examining how the algorithm mediates, and exacerbates, the polycrisis.

## Positions
- Technology no longer sits between people and the world; it is the way the world arrives.
- A generation has grown up digital-first, learning social norms inside engagement-maximising platforms and carrying them back into the physical world.
- Mediation changes language, then perception, then what is taken to be normal, possible and real (e.g. distance now measured in minutes because of maps).

## Method
Structured first-person accounts collected under a fixed protocol, compared across generations and geographies, published in full with working papers.

## Programme
Interventions at personal, institutional and societal scale; new institutions for a post-scarcity society.

## Figures
- [Figures](https://postphenom.com/figures): six interactive figures — what coexists, the distribution of taste, the influence graph, precedence, directionally correct, the arbitration.
- [Reading the Figures](https://postphenom.com/figures/legend): what each figure claims, what every animation means, and an audit of which claims are grounded.
- [What You Study](https://postphenom.com/position): thesis, the fields it maps to, and a manifesto.
